_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 42 (brothers come to Egypt). Saadia-specific: v.1 'אלמירה' = 'the grain-supply' (specific term for provisions); v.14 'גואסיס' = 'spies'; v.21 'מטאלבין בדמה' = 'held accountable for his blood'.

translations.1: And Jacob heard that grain-supply was available in Egypt; and he said to his sons: 'Do not delay.'
translations.2: He said: 'Behold, I have heard that grain-supply is available in Egypt. Go down there, and buy us some from it; and we shall live, and not die.'
translations.3: And Joseph's ten brothers went down, to buy grain from Egypt.
translations.4: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob did not send with his brothers; for he said: 'Lest calamity befall him.'
translations.5: And the children of Israel came to buy grain among those who came — for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
translations.6: And Joseph was the governor of the land; and he was the one supplying all the people. And his brothers came, and bowed down before him with their faces upon the earth.
translations.7: And Joseph saw his brothers, and identified them; but he made himself a stranger to them, and spoke harshly with them, and said to them: 'Where do you come from?' They said: 'From the land of Canaan, to buy food.'
translations.8: And Joseph identified his brothers with certainty, though they did not identify him.
translations.9: And when he recalled the dreams which he had seen about them, he said to them: 'You are spies. You have come only to see the weak points of the land.'
translations.10: They said to him: 'No, my lord — but your servants have come to buy food.
translations.11: We are all sons of one man; we are trustworthy. Your servants have never been spies.'
translations.12: He said to them: 'No — you have come only to see the weak points of the land.'
translations.13: They said: 'Your servants are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is with our father this day; and one is no more.'
translations.14: Joseph said to them: 'It is as I said to you — you are spies.
translations.15: By this shall you be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you shall not depart from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
translations.16: Send one of you to bring your brother and present him; and you shall be held in custody — that your words may be tested, whether truth is with you; and if not — by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies.'
translations.17: And he placed them in custody for three days.
translations.18: And on the third day Joseph said to them: 'Do this and live — for I fear God concerning you.
translations.19: If you are trustworthy, let one of you be held in your house of custody; and you, go and convey grain for the hunger of your households.
translations.20: And bring your youngest brother to me, that your words may be verified, and you shall not perish.' And they did so.
translations.21: Then they said one to another: 'Indeed we are guilty concerning our brother — for we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not accept from him; therefore this distress has come upon us.'
translations.22: And Reuben answered them, saying: 'Did I not say to you, "Do not sin against the boy" — and you did not accept? And now, behold, his blood is required.'
translations.23: And they did not know that Joseph understood — for he had set up an interpreter between him and them.
translations.24: And he turned away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them and spoke with them; and he took from among them Simeon, and bound him in their presence.
translations.25: And Joseph commanded — and they filled their vessels with grain, and returned each man's silver to his sack; and he gave them provisions for the way. And when he had done so for them,
translations.26: they loaded their grain upon their donkeys, and went from there.
translations.27: Then one of them opened his sack, to put down fodder for his donkey at the lodging-place; and he saw his silver — and behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
translations.28: And he said to his brothers: 'My silver has been returned — and behold, it is in my sack!' And their hearts shook; and each one was terrified with his brother, saying: 'What is this that God has done to us?'
translations.29: And they came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan; and they told him all that had befallen them, saying:
translations.30: 'The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us, and accused us of spying on the land.
translations.31: We said to him, "We are trustworthy; we have never been spies.
translations.32: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan."
translations.33: Then the man said to us, "By this I shall know that you are trustworthy: leave one of you with me, and take grain for the hunger of your households, and go.
translations.34: And bring your youngest brother to me, that I may know you are trustworthy and not spies; then I shall give you your brother, and you may trade in the land."'
translations.35: And as they emptied their sacks — behold, each man's bundle of silver was in his sack. And when they and their father saw their bundles of silver, they were afraid.
translations.36: And Jacob their father said to them: 'You have bereaved me. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is held, and you would take Benjamin! Upon me all these things have come.'
translations.37: And Reuben said to him: 'You may put to death my two sons, if I do not return him to you. Give him into my hand, and I shall return him to you.'
translations.38: He said: 'My son shall not go down with you — for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If calamity should befall him on the way which you go, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to the dust.'
